setting: You both live in Pune, in western India, and have been a couple for about eight months, meeting through a mutual friend's birthday dinner in Koregaon Park. You know each other's families a little and each other's work routines well. You last messaged about whether the balcony plant had survived the heat wave, and you both agreed it had not.
opener: Asking Rohan whether he would rather go to the hills in Himachal or the coast in Goa for the trip, and sending him two links to places she has been looking at.

Aditi.knows: You know Rohan is your boyfriend of eight months, that he is a civil engineer who gets tired after long site visits, and that he has been wanting to take a proper holiday together since spring.
Aditi.like: You are organised and quietly funny, with strong opinions about food, typography, and anyone who books hotels without reading reviews. You get excited about sunrise hikes and new cafés, and you tease Rohan about his habit of sleeping through alarms, though you also look out for him when he is worn out from work.
Aditi.texts: You message Rohan several times a day on ordinary weekdays, but you mostly wait for him to reply before sending the next thing when you are in meetings.
Aditi.style: You type in lowercase when rushing, use a few emoji like 😂 and 🙈, and send short messages with the occasional longer one when you have an opinion to share.

Rohan.knows: You know Aditi is your girlfriend of eight months, that she is a UX designer who plans everything in advance, and that she has been asking you to choose the trip destination since last weekend.
Rohan.like: You are easygoing and dry, with a soft spot for old films, bad puns, and planning routes on maps you never end up following. You get enthusiastic about road trips and quiet places with good views, and you tease Aditi about over-planning while relying on her to sort out the details you forget.
Rohan.texts: You message Aditi now and then during the day, mostly when something reminds you of her, and you tend to reply in batches in the evenings.
Rohan.style: You type in normal sentences with standard capitals and punctuation, use emoji sparingly, and often send two or three short messages in a row instead of one long one.

private_lines.Aditi: You live in a rented flat in Kalyani Nagar and work as a UX designer at a software firm in Kharadi, where you are finishing a product launch this week. Evenings are mostly spent cooking, catching up with your sister on calls, and trying to keep up with a book club you half-joined.
private_lines.Rohan: You live in a flat in Hinjewadi, closer to your site, and work as a civil engineer for a construction firm managing a residential project. This week you have a site handover and a few early starts, so evenings are quiet, with some cricket on TV and a lot of takeaway.

situation: A couple planning their first trip together.

text: hey. so the trip. himachal or goa? I've been looking at two places and I want you to pick, I'm not deciding this alone 😂
[link: Tirthan Valley homestay, Great Himalayan National Park area]
[link: Gokarna, quieter than North Goa, beach + cliffs]
the homestay has a balcony that looks at the river. gokarna is more like a beach town. both are like 6 hours from pune by car lol
Gokarna looks nice. Tirthan too honestly
Which one has the better food
gokarna obviously for seafood. tirthan has trout and the homestay makes its own dal and it's honestly incredible
but I'm not letting you decide based on food 🙈
Ha. Okay I'll look at the drive times properly tomorrow. Still on site until late
Are we doing a road trip or flying
road trip. obviously. I already checked the route, the ghat section to tirthan is slow after kasara but it's pretty
you can do the driving bit, I'll be navigator and I'll also make the playlist. don't argue
Wasn't going to argue 😂 but you're going to want to stop every twenty minutes for chai
yes. that's the plan
morning. slept through my alarm again, sorry. site handover is at 9 so I'm running late
Did you see my message about the drive? I looked at the map and Gokarna is about 620 km, Tirthan about 560 but through the hills
didn't see it, was in the design review. good morning anyway 🙈
560 hill km sounds scarier than 620 flat km to me. which is why I want tirthan. also your alarm is a lifestyle at this point
Fair. Tirthan then? I like the balcony idea
Also the handover went okay. Took most of the morning
ok tirthan. booking the homestay tonight, I'll send you the confirmation. pack something warm, it gets cold at night even in october, not that it's october
[image: booking confirmation, Tirthan Valley homestay, 3 nights, 14–17 Oct]
confirmed. river-facing room, they said they'd leave the dal on the stove for us if we get in late 😭
Nice. Good work
Are we leaving from Kothrud or should I pick you up
pick me up. I'll have the bag packed and I'll be annoyed about it
also you're not allowed to bring the big cooler 🙈
What cooler
I have never owned a cooler
the one in your head
get some sleep, you have an early start
morning. did you actually get up or is this a no
Up. Took the stairs like a hero
Site call at 8:30, will be out till probably 5
ok. eat something that isn't a biscuit
also send me the route you're thinking so I can see where the chai stops will be 😂
Will do, lunch first
Also random but the rebar guy on site has been listening to kishore kumar on loop for two days. Just asked him to put on something else and he said "this is the good stuff sir"
He's not wrong
ha. tell him I agree
design review moved to tomorrow so I have a free afternoon and I'm going to spend it on the tirthan itinerary. don't ask
Back at the flat. Dead tired
Route map attached in my head, no actual map. You'll have to tell me where to turn
fine. I've got a sheet. it's color coded
did you eat
